chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal informed us, from his father, who said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever seeks the forgiveness of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, seventy times in Sha'ban, Allah will forgive his sins, even if they were similar in number to the stars.

key_terms.استغفر: Istighfar - seeking God's forgiveness, a fundamental act of worship involving acknowledging sin and requesting divine pardon
key_terms.النجوم: Stars - used as a metaphor for an innumerable quantity, emphasizing the vastness of God's forgiveness
key_terms.ذنوب: Dhunub (sins) - transgressions against divine law, whether major or minor
key_terms.شعبان: Sha'ban - the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, preceding Ramadan, with special spiritual significance

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for seeking forgiveness in the month of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) taught that seeking God's forgiveness (istighfar) seventy times during the month of Sha'ban guarantees divine pardon, even for sins as numerous as the stars. This hadith was narrated in the context of highlighting the spiritual merits of Sha'ban, the month preceding Ramadan, which the Prophet and his family particularly emphasized as a time of preparation and repentance. The hyperbolic comparison to the number of stars underscores God's boundless mercy.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
